issues.description: The solution implementation of set_pixel introduces an unexpected dependency on the EDI register (an alpha-channel presence check: 'or edi, edi' / 'jz .skip_alpha') which is not mentioned in the problem statement or the template. Because of this conditional, the address computation path differs depending on the caller's EDI value and can produce an incorrect address (and thus wrong pixel writes/reads) when EDI is zero. The problem statement requires that x is passed in EAX, y in EBX and the color in ECX and does not define or permit any implicit parameter in EDI. The presence of this extra implicit dependency in the solution is an unintentional mismatch that will confuse students and can make the reference implementation behave incorrectly in some cases.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the EDI-dependent alpha-channel check from the solution's set_pixel implementation. Ensure the function computes the pixel address solely from EAX (x) and EBX (y) and writes ECX to that address. Preserve registers as required by the spec (only EAX may be changed on return). If alpha-channel support is intended, document it in the problem statement and make it an explicit parameter instead of relying on an implicit EDI dependency.
